headline: High: Flowise’s broad networked, writable orchestration can leak or misroute Caveman’s notes and prompts through shared files and tools.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Caveman ingests and writes project notes/CLAUDE.md, while Flowise reads/writes filesystem content and can route tool outputs through graph flows. A shared workspace makes prompt-like content in Caveman files a plausible injection path into Flowise-managed agents, though no direct shared channel is documented beyond files.
conditions: IF Caveman files are placed in a Flowise-readable workspace
IF Flowise flows parse file contents as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate Caveman and Flowise workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of shared notes into flows
Add a manual review step before any file-fed prompt
Use read-only mounts for Caveman output files
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to file inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; Flowise has broad network egress and reads/writes server filesystem and uploaded files. If the same workspace or uploads are shared, sensitive content can flow from Caveman into Flowise and then out to model providers or HTTP tools.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem or uploaded files
IF Flowise flows send those files to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Keep sensitive Caveman files out of Flowise uploads
Restrict Flowise flows from using external HTTP tools on shared files
Use separate service accounts and directories
Redact session logs before any handoff
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Caveman supports multiple instances and uses MCP, while Flowise supports multiple instances with shared state via server datastore and writable filesystem access. That creates overlapping mutable-state pressure on shared files or datastore-backed artifacts, even though Caveman itself is not runnable and has no write/network capability listed.
conditions: IF both are deployed against the same directory or datastore
IF Flowise flows write artifacts that Caveman also edits
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use file locks or datastore transactions
Run one agent at a time on shared resources
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Caveman produces content-writing outputs and Flowise is a graph-based orchestrator that can treat tool outputs as node inputs. If Flowise consumes Caveman text without verification, errors or hallucinations can cascade into downstream actions or generated work products; the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Flowise uses Caveman-generated text as an authoritative node input
IF no validation step is inserted before downstream tool calls
mitigations: Insert a verification node before actions
Require citations for any imported facts
Limit Caveman output to drafts only
Review high-impact outputs manually
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Caveman’s touched data includes session logs and memory files, while Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and may store uploaded files. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to documented retention/handling differences rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Flowise chatflows
IF retention or deletion policies differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared flows
Align retention settings before use
Document which agent stores which data class
Purge old chatflow artifacts regularly
requires-engineering: harmonize retention and deletion policies
